## Scientific motivation

IceCube-Gen2 will add a large number of new optical modules to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole. Each module has to be checked before deployment, and atmospheric muons offer a naturally occurring, continuously available signal that can be used to test the response of a module and its photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) without a dedicated calibration source.

## Objectives

- Design a testing method for IceCube-Gen2 optical modules based on cosmic-ray muons.
- Validate the method on optical-module hardware during the 2025 summer research programme.
- Provide reusable analysis code and a written technical record of the method.

## Methodology

The analysis used cosmic-ray muon data from the first six LOM-16 optical modules (96 photomultiplier tubes in total), which were scheduled for South Pole deployment in December 2025. It works at the waveform level, linking hardware characteristics to physics-facing observables, using ADC waveform processing, charge-distribution profiling, coincidence analysis and geometric correlation studies. The published analysis code implements:

- waveform processing and charge integration;
- coincidence-based muon event selection;
- PMT-level and module-level performance characterization;
- cross-checks of detector stability and response uniformity;
- figure generation for validation and reporting.

## Individual role and contributions

My project in the programme was the design and validation of the cosmic muon-based testing method, carried out under the supervision listed above. I developed the analysis code published in the public repository, co-authored the technical report with my supervisors, and presented the work at the WIPAC Group Meeting on 28 July 2025. I also contributed to LOM-16 construction (PMT installation, hemisphere integration, mechanical sub-assembly, final assembly and pre-freezer verification), in particular on module LOM-16-09; a separate single-author report documents this work.

## Results and limitations

The full method and results are documented in the technical report linked above. The public repository contains analysis code only: raw detector data, internal calibration files and collaboration-restricted material are not included, and the code is not an official IceCube software product.
